observations.explanation: The paper describes ten datasets across arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning (pp. 2, 4–5). Its reported comparisons show PS+ outperforming Zero-shot-CoT across those datasets (pp. 5–6).

The prompt comparison reports that the variable-extraction-only Prompt 3 performs worse than Zero-shot-CoT Prompt 1, while prompts adding planning and further instructions perform better (pp. 6–7). This supports the qualified claim that the ablation provides evidence, though it does not isolate every instruction’s effect.
The limitations section explicitly says semantic misunderstanding errors remain and that the authors plan to explore addressing them (p. 9).

The main-paper results use text-davinci-003 (p. 5), but the paper also says text-davinci-002 experiment results are in the appendix (p. 5; appendix overview, p. 11). The evidence does not establish generalization across model families, but the broad implication that version generalization is wholly untested overlooks the stated 002 results.
